definition_en: still happening or continuing, and not yet finished or settled

scene: 这里指「持续进行的」。 An ongoing investigation kept the office busy through the winter.

senses.title: Still going: continuing without a stop
senses.definition: continuing to happen or develop, without having stopped
senses.definitionCN: 继续发生或发展，并没有停下来
senses.example: The river is an ongoing source of power for the village.
senses.exampleCN: 这条河一直是村子持续不断的动力来源。
senses.why: Ongoing is simply on 'continuing' plus going 'walking'. The picture is someone still on the road, one step after another, with no arrival and no halt.
senses.whyCN: ongoing 就是 on“继续”加 going“走”。画面是一个人仍在路上，一步一步，既没有到达，也没有停歇。

senses.title: In progress now: an ongoing investigation
senses.titleCN: 进行中：此刻仍在办的调查
senses.definition: currently being carried out, used of work that has started and is not yet over
senses.definitionCN: 目前正在被执行，用于已经开始而尚未结束的工作
senses.example: An ongoing investigation kept the office busy through the winter.
senses.exampleCN: 一项仍在进行的调查让办公室忙了一整个冬天。
senses.why: The walking is happening at this moment. English uses ongoing for official work precisely because the result is not in yet: the case is still on the road.
senses.whyCN: “走”正发生在此刻。英语用 ongoing 形容公务，正因为结果还没出来：案子还在路上。

senses.title: Not yet finished: an ongoing project
senses.titleCN: 尚未完成：还在做的项目
senses.definition: not completed, used of a task, building or piece of work still under way
senses.definitionCN: 尚未完成，用于仍在施工或推进的任务、工程
senses.example: The ongoing bridge repairs will last until spring.
senses.exampleCN: 仍在进行的桥梁维修会持续到春天。
senses.why: If the walk has not ended, the destination has not been reached. Not finishing is the negative face of the same continuing motion.
senses.whyCN: 如果行走没有结束，终点就还没到达。“未完成”是同一段持续运动的否定面。

senses.title: Continuing over a long period: ongoing support
senses.definition: continuing for a long time, often of help, care or relationships
senses.definitionCN: 长时间持续，常用于帮助、照护或关系
senses.example: The charity offers ongoing support to families after the flood.
senses.exampleCN: 洪灾过后，这家慈善机构为家庭提供持续支持。
senses.why: Here the road is long and the walking steady: help that does not stop after the first emergency but keeps pace with the family.
senses.whyCN: 这里路很长，脚步很稳：帮助不是应急一次就结束，而是与这个家庭同步走下去。

senses.title: Recurring regularly: ongoing costs
senses.definition: recurring again and again rather than happening once, used of costs, duties and maintenance
senses.definitionCN: 一次又一次地反复出现而非只发生一次，用于费用、职责与维护
senses.example: Ongoing costs include rent, insurance and repairs.
senses.exampleCN: 持续费用包括房租、保险和维修。
senses.why: A single payment ends; a cost that keeps coming is a walk that keeps returning to the same stretch of road, so the adjective marks repetition as well as duration.
senses.whyCN: 一次性付款会结束；不断出现的费用则像总回到同一段路上的行走，因此这个形容词既标持续时间，也标反复。

senses.title: Gradual and continuing: ongoing decline
senses.titleCN: 逐步而持续：不断加剧的衰退
senses.definition: continuing steadily in one direction, used of changes that develop over time
senses.definitionCN: 朝一个方向稳定持续，用于随时间发展的变化
senses.example: The ongoing decline in rainfall worries local farmers.
senses.exampleCN: 降雨量持续下降让当地农民担忧。
senses.why: A slow change is still motion: the walk continues in the same direction, and the lack of a stop is what makes the trend serious.
senses.whyCN: 缓慢的变化仍是运动：行走朝同一方向继续，而“不停”正是这种趋势令人担忧的原因。

senses.title: Medical: a condition still present
senses.titleCN: 医学用法：症状仍然存在
senses.definition: still present after treatment or over time, used of symptoms and conditions
senses.definitionCN: 在治疗后或经过一段时间仍然存在，用于症状与病情
senses.example: Patients reported ongoing pain six months after the surgery.
senses.exampleCN: 患者表示术后六个月仍有持续疼痛。
senses.why: In medicine the walk is the symptom's course: it has not stopped, so the condition is not resolved and must still be managed.
senses.whyCN: 在医学里，行走就是症状的病程：它没有停下，所以病情未解除，仍需处理。

senses.title: A process with no clear end point
senses.definition: used of processes that have no natural finish and simply keep developing
senses.definitionCN: 用于没有天然终点、只是一直发展下去的过程
senses.example: Language change is an ongoing process, not a project with a deadline.
senses.exampleCN: 语言变化是一个持续的过程，不是有截止日期的项目。
senses.why: Some roads have no gate at the end. When a process cannot be completed by definition, ongoing names its permanent condition rather than a temporary stage.
senses.whyCN: 有些路尽头没有门。当一个过程按定义就无法完成时，ongoing 命名的是它的永久状态，而不是某个临时阶段。

senses.title: Unresolved: an ongoing debate
senses.titleCN: 未有定论：仍在争的辩论
senses.definition: still being argued or decided, used of disputes and questions without a settled answer
senses.definitionCN: 仍在争论或决定中，用于没有定论的争议与问题
senses.example: Whether to build the dam remains an ongoing debate.
senses.exampleCN: 是否修建大坝仍是一场未有定论的争论。
senses.why: The walking here is argument going back and forth. Because no side has stopped, the question is still open and the debate is ongoing.
senses.whyCN: 这里的行走是来回往复的争论。因为没有一方停下，问题仍未闭合，辩论便处于 ongoing 状态。

intro.en: Ongoing is a modern English compound recorded from 1877: on 'continuing' plus going 'walking'. It is not a classical root word, and no Latin ancestry should be invented for it.
intro.cn: ongoing 是 1877 年有记录的现代英语复合词：on“继续”加 going“走”。它不是古典词根词，不应为它编造拉丁来源。

items.en: Ongoing is first recorded in 1877 as an adjective meaning 'continuing, still in progress'.
items.cn: ongoing 于 1877 年首次被记录为形容词，意为“继续的、仍在进行的”。

items.en: The word is on 'on, onward' plus going, the present participle of go: literally 'going on'.
items.cn: 这个词由 on“继续、向前”加 going（go 的现在分词）构成，字面就是“一直走着”。

items.en: Going is a gerund formed around 1300 from go. Old English had no such form; its inherited noun for a journey was gang.
items.cn: going 是约 1300 年由 go 构成的动名词。古英语没有这个形式，它固有的表示“行程”的名词是 gang。

items.en: The verb go continues Old English gān 'to go, walk'; its past went comes from a different verb, wendan 'to turn, go'.
items.cn: 动词 go 继承古英语 gān“走、行走”；它的过去式 went 来自另一个动词 wendan“转、去”。

items.en: In the 20th century ongoing spreads into administration, finance, medicine and journalism: ongoing investigation, ongoing costs, ongoing symptoms.
items.cn: 20 世纪，ongoing 扩展到行政、金融、医学与新闻语言：ongoing investigation、ongoing costs、ongoing symptoms。

items.en: Both ongoing and the hyphenated on-going are used today; the solid spelling is now standard in most styles.
items.cn: 今天 ongoing 与带连字符的 on-going 两种写法都在用；多数体例以连写为标准。

note.en: The first group is chosen for spelling and sound, the second for meaning, so that form and sense stay separate.
note.cn: 第一组按拼写和读音挑选，第二组按词义挑选，这样词形和词义不会混在一起。

entries.definition: coming toward you, as of traffic. It shares on- but means approaching, not continuing.
entries.definitionCN: 迎面而来的，如车流。它同样以 on- 开头，但意思是“接近”，不是“持续”。

entries.definition: friendly and sociable, or leaving a place. It joins out- to going and has nothing to do with continuation.
entries.definitionCN: 外向友善的；离去的。它把 out- 加在 going 上，与“持续”无关。

entries.definition: the act of leaving, or the condition of travel. It is the participle on which ongoing is built.
entries.definitionCN: 离开；行走状况。它是构成 ongoing 的分词本身。

entries.definition: going on without any interruption. It is stricter than ongoing, which allows pauses and repetition.
entries.definitionCN: 毫无中断地进行。它比 ongoing 更严格，后者允许停顿与反复。

entries.definition: still carrying on after a start. It is close to ongoing but sounds more like a description of an action than a label.
entries.definitionCN: 开始之后仍在继续。它与 ongoing 接近，但更像描述动作，而非贴标签。

entries.definition: not completed. It states the missing end, while ongoing states the continuing motion.
entries.definitionCN: 尚未完成。它说的是缺少结尾，ongoing 说的是持续的运动。

normalIntro.en: These links are real: on plus going, the verb go and its participle, and the fixed phrases ongoing investigation and ongoing costs.
normalIntro.cn: 这些联想都是真实的：on + going、动词 go 及其分词，以及固定搭配 ongoing investigation、ongoing costs。

normal.en: on 'onward' plus going 'walking' gives 'walking on': the person has not stopped and has not arrived.
normal.cn: on“向前”加 going“走”就是“一直走”：人既没停，也没到。

normal.en: Going is the present participle of go, so ongoing is built from an everyday verb rather than a Latin root.
normal.cn: going 是 go 的现在分词，因此 ongoing 是由日常动词构成，而非拉丁词根。

normal.en: Old English gang also meant 'a going, journey'; going replaced it as the ordinary noun.
normal.cn: 古英语 gang 也指“行走、旅程”；going 后来取代它成为普通名词。

normal.en: An ongoing investigation is a case still on the road, with no result yet.
normal.cn: an ongoing investigation 是仍在路上的案子，结果还没出来。

normal.en: Ongoing costs are payments that keep returning, like a walk that keeps coming back to the same stretch.
normal.cn: ongoing costs 是不断回来的支出，像总回到同一段路上的行走。

abstract.en: Picture a walker on a road with no gate in sight: the only fact about him is that he is still walking.
abstract.cn: 想象一个行者走在望不见门的路上：关于他的唯一事实就是还在走。

abstract.en: The walk can be a case, a bridge, a decline, a pain, or an argument; what they share is that the motion has not stopped.
abstract.cn: 这段行走可以是一桩案子、一座桥、一场衰退、一处疼痛或一场争论；共同点是运动没有停止。

abstract.en: When the road has no end by nature, ongoing stops describing a stage and names a permanent condition.
abstract.cn: 当路本身就没有尽头，ongoing 便不再描述某个阶段，而是在命名一种永久状态。

examples.en: The archive is an ongoing project that will take another decade.
examples.cn: 这项档案工程仍在进行，还要再花十年。

examples.en: Ongoing repairs have closed one lane of the bridge since March.
examples.cn: 自三月起，持续进行的维修封住了桥的一条车道。

examples.en: Their ongoing disagreement about the budget delayed the vote.
examples.cn: 他们在预算上持续不断的分歧推迟了表决。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「昂，够硬」——昂，够硬！这工程一直在进行，从来没停过 → ongoing 持续进行的

root: 现代英语复合词 on“继续、向前”+ going“走”（go 的现在分词，go 继承古英语 gān“行走”），1877 年始见记录；与古典词根无关。

sensesIntro.en: Nine senses of ongoing all start from one picture: a walker still on the road. The same continuing motion then covers official work, unfinished projects, long-term help, recurring costs, slow trends, symptoms, endless processes and open arguments.
sensesIntro.cn: ongoing 的九个义项都从同一幅画出发：一个行者仍在路上。同一段持续运动随后覆盖公务、未完成的工程、长期帮助、反复费用、缓慢趋势、症状、无尽过程与未有定论的争论。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a walker still moving along the same road, with no stop and no arrival.
core.cn: 核心意象：行者沿着同一条路继续走，既没有停，也没有到。

branches.en: THE WALK ITSELF: motion that continues, including processes that have no end point at all.
branches.cn: 行走本身：持续不断的运动，也包括根本没有终点的过程。

branches.en: WORK UNDER WAY: an investigation or a project that has started and has not finished.
branches.cn: 在办之事：已经启动而尚未结束的调查或工程。

branches.en: THE LONG ROAD: help that keeps pace over years, and costs that keep returning.
branches.cn: 长路：经年同步的支持，以及不断回来的费用。

branches.en: THE STEADY COURSE: a trend that keeps moving one way, and a symptom that has not stopped.
branches.cn: 稳定的走向：一直朝一个方向推进的趋势，以及没有停下的症状。

branches.en: THE OPEN QUESTION: a debate still going back and forth with no settled answer.
branches.cn: 未决之问：仍在来回、没有定论的辩论。

intro.en: Ongoing is a native English compound of on plus the present participle going, with no Latin prefix. English adds -ly and -ness to it, and the same going also appears in outgoing and easygoing.
intro.cn: ongoing 是英语本土复合词，由 on 加现在分词 going 构成，没有拉丁前缀。英语又给它加 -ly、-ness，同一个 going 也出现在 outgoing、easygoing 中。

latinIntro.en: There is no Latin source for ongoing. Its oldest forms are Germanic: Old English gān 'to go' and the noun gang 'a going, journey'. The entries below give those forms rather than Latin words.
latinIntro.cn: ongoing 没有拉丁语来源。它最早的形式属于日耳曼语：古英语 gān“走”和名词 gang“行走、旅程”。下面给出这些形式，而不是拉丁词。

items.structure: on- (on, onward) + going (present participle of go)
items.meaning: still going on; continuing and not finished
items.meaningCN: 仍在进行的；持续的；未结束的
items.example: The cleanup is ongoing after the storm.
items.exampleCN: 风暴过后的清理仍在进行。

items.meaningCN: 持续地；不间断地（罕用，-ly 构成副词）
items.example: The team meets ongoingly to review the case.
items.exampleCN: 团队持续开会复审此案。

items.meaningCN: 持续性；进行状态（罕用，-ness 构成名词）
items.example: The ongoingness of the war exhausted both sides.
items.exampleCN: 战争的持续不断让双方都筋疲力尽。

items.meaning: the act of leaving or travelling; that which goes
items.meaningCN: 离开；行走；进行中的（go 的动名词与分词）
items.example: The going was slow on the wet track.
items.exampleCN: 在湿滑的小路上走得很慢。

items.meaning: events or activities, often suspicious ones
items.meaningCN: 发生的活动；（常指可疑的）勾当
items.example: She wanted to know about the goings-on next door.
items.exampleCN: 她想知道隔壁在搞什么名堂。

items.meaningCN: 外向的；离去的（out-“向外”+ going）
items.example: He is the most outgoing member of the team.
items.exampleCN: 他是队里最外向的成员。

items.example: Her easygoing manner calms the whole office.
items.exampleCN: 她随和的态度让整个办公室都安定下来。

items.meaning: to experience or pass through something
items.meaningCN: 经历；经受（under- + go“走”，即从下面走过）
items.example: The building will undergo major repairs.

items.structure: go (bare verb from Old English gān)
items.meaning: to move from one place to another
items.example: They go to the market every Saturday.

latinEntries.meaningCN: 行走；旅程；通道；进程（古英语）

definition_zh: 公开地；不隐瞒地；当众；坦率地
definition_en: in a way that does not hide facts, feelings or intentions and can be seen or heard by other people
core_image: 一扇原本关着的窗被推开，屋里的东西全暴露在日光下
scene: 会议进行到一半，一位年轻工程师站起来，把项目失败的原因一条条讲出来，没有替任何人遮掩。He spoke openly about the delays that had ruined the schedule.
sceneCN: 这里是「公开地、不隐瞒地」（第 1 个义项：不掩饰事实或态度）；句意为他把拖垮进度的延误坦然讲了出来。图中可辨识物件：推开的窗、照进屋内的日光、摊开的文件。

pos.zh: 公开地；不隐瞒地；当众；坦率地

derivatives.zh: 由形容词 open 加名词后缀 -ness 构成，义为「公开；坦率；开阔」
由动词 open 加 -ing 构成，义为「开口；开幕；空缺职位」
由 open 加表示「做某事的人或物」的 -er 构成，义为「开启者；开瓶器」

senses.title: Without hiding the facts
senses.definition: in a way that lets other people see or know the facts instead of keeping them secret
senses.definitionCN: 让他人看到或知道事实，而不是把事实藏起来
senses.example: She openly admitted that the first draft had failed.
senses.exampleCN: 她公开承认初稿失败了。
senses.why: Open describes something not shut and not covered, so acting openly means leaving the facts uncovered for anyone to look at.
senses.whyCN: open 形容没有关闭、没有遮盖的东西，所以 openly 做事就是把事实摊开任人查看，而不是盖上一块布。

senses.title: In front of other people
senses.definition: in public, where other people can see or hear what happens
senses.definitionCN: 在公开场合，别人能够看见或听见所发生的事
senses.example: The two ministers openly disagreed in front of the press.
senses.exampleCN: 两位部长在记者面前公开表示意见不合。
senses.why: If nothing is covered, the act cannot stay private, so the same picture of an open space turns into doing something in public.
senses.whyCN: 既然没有遮盖，这个动作就留不住私密性；同一种「空间敞开」的画面，自然转到「当众做事」的含义上。

senses.title: Frankly, with feelings shown
senses.definition: in a direct way that shows real feelings or intentions without disguise
senses.definitionCN: 直接表达真实情感或意图，不加伪装
senses.example: They openly wept when the old theatre was pulled down.
senses.exampleCN: 那座老剧院被拆时，他们毫不掩饰地哭了。
senses.why: The image stretches from objects to feelings: a face that hides nothing is as open as a door that has never been locked.
senses.whyCN: 这个意象从物体延伸到情感：一张不藏东西的脸，就像一扇从没上过锁的门那样「敞开」。

intro.en: Openly is the adjective open plus the adverb suffix -ly, so its history is the history of open, a native English and Germanic word rather than a Latin one.
intro.cn: openly 就是形容词 open 加副词后缀 -ly，它的历史就是 open 的历史，而 open 是英语本土的日耳曼词，并非来自拉丁语。

items.en: The reconstructed root *upanaz is generally tied to the idea of being up or lifted, and it is the source of the English word for not shut.
items.cn: 一般认为，重构词根 *upanaz 与「向上、抬起」的意思相关，是英语中表示「未关闭」这个词的来源。

items.en: Old English already had open as an adjective for what is not closed, not covered or not blocked.
items.cn: 古英语里已有 open 这个形容词，表示未关闭、未遮盖或未被阻挡。

items.en: Middle English added -ly to adjectives to build adverbs, and openly appeared as the manner word for open action.
items.cn: 中古英语用 -ly 把形容词变成副词，openly 就这样出现，表示「以敞开的方式」。

items.en: The adverb moved from physical openings to speech, so saying something openly meant saying it with nothing concealed.
items.cn: 这个副词从物理上的敞开扩展到言语，说某事 openly 就是一点不隐瞒地说。

items.en: Modern English uses openly mainly for facts, feelings and public disagreement, and speak openly has become the usual pairing.
items.cn: 现代英语的 openly 主要用于事实、情感和公开的分歧，speak openly 已成为最常见的搭配。

note.en: The look-alike group keeps the open family and its spellings; the near-meaning group keeps adverbs that describe how plainly something is said or done.
note.cn: 形近组收 open 词族的同根词与不同拼写；近义组收同样描述「说得或做得有多直白」的副词。

entries.definition: The adjective behind openly, meaning not closed and not hidden.
entries.definitionCN: openly 所由构成的形容词，义为未关闭、不隐瞒的。

entries.definition: A hole or gap, or the first performance of a show.
entries.definitionCN: 开口或缺口的；也指演出的首场。

entries.definition: The quality of being open, honest or free to enter.
entries.definitionCN: 公开、坦诚或可自由进入的性质。

entries.definition: Generous, with the hand open to give.
entries.definitionCN: 慷慨大方的，手掌张开愿意给予。

entries.definition: In a direct and honest way, with no attempt to hide anything.
entries.definitionCN: 直接而诚实，不试图隐瞒任何东西。

entries.definition: In a place or manner that everyone can see or know.
entries.definitionCN: 在人人可见可知的场合或方式下。

entries.definition: Honestly, even when the truth makes people uncomfortable.
entries.definitionCN: 诚实地说，即使真相让人不舒服。

normalIntro.en: The word is open plus -ly, so every mnemonic hangs on the picture of something uncovered and on the small family built from the same adjective.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词就是 open 加 -ly，所以联想都围绕「没有遮盖」的画面，以及由同一形容词长出的那一小族词。

normal.en: Open means not shut, so openly means with nothing shut away.
normal.cn: open 是「没关上」，openly 就是「没把任何东西关起来藏住」。

normal.en: -ly turns the adjective into a manner, so an open act becomes an act done openly.
normal.cn: -ly 把形容词变成方式，于是 open 的动作就成了 openly 地做。

normal.en: Openness is the noun of the same family, naming the same quality as a thing.
normal.cn: openness 是同一词族的名词形式，把同一种性质当成一个东西来说。

normal.en: An opening is the place where something has been opened: a gap or a first night.
normal.cn: opening 是被打开的地方：一个缺口，或一场首演。

normal.en: Speak openly is the most common pairing, because speech is where hiding is easiest.
normal.cn: speak openly 是最常见的搭配，因为言语最容易把东西藏住。

abstract.en: A window pushed up in the morning: the room has nothing left to hide.
abstract.cn: 清晨把窗子推上去：屋子再没有可以藏的东西。

abstract.en: A closed hand keeps a secret, while an open hand must show what it holds.
abstract.cn: 握紧的手能藏住秘密，张开的手只能让人看见掌心里的东西。

abstract.en: Saying a hard truth openly costs more than saying an easy one quietly.
abstract.cn: 把难听的真相公开说出来，比轻声说一句好听话代价更大。

examples.en: She openly admitted that the first draft had failed.
examples.cn: 她公开承认初稿失败了。

examples.en: The committee openly rejected the proposal.
examples.cn: 委员会公开否决了这项提议。

examples.en: He prefers to speak openly rather than hint at problems.
examples.cn: 他宁愿把问题直说，也不愿只做暗示。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「欧盆里」——盆盖一掀开，里面的东西全看得见；记住 openly 是公开地。

root: open 属英语本土的日耳曼词，一般认为来自重构词根 *upanaz（向上、抬起）；加 -ly 构成副词 openly，义为「以敞开、不遮掩的方式」。这个词没有可靠的拉丁同族词。

sensesIntro.en: The core is an uncovered surface, and the senses move from facts that are not hidden, to acts done in public, to feelings shown without disguise.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是「没有遮盖的表面」；义项从「不隐瞒的事实」移到「在人前做的事」，再到「不加伪装地流露情感」。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a window pushed open so that everything inside stands in plain light.
core.cn: 核心意象：一扇被推开的窗，屋里的一切都摆在明处。

branches.en: a draft read aloud with the failed pages left in
branches.cn: 朗读稿子时把失败的页码照样留在里面

branches.en: a manager naming the delay instead of blaming the weather
branches.cn: 负责人直接点出延误，而不是怪天气

branches.en: two officials arguing in front of reporters
branches.cn: 两位官员在记者面前争论

branches.en: a face that will not look away while speaking
branches.cn: 说话时不肯把脸转开

branches.en: mourners weeping without turning aside
branches.cn: 送别的人不侧过脸就哭了出来

intro.en: The word is a Germanic adjective for not shut plus the English adverb suffix -ly, and the family around it adds nouns for the gap, the act and the quality.
intro.cn: 这个词由表示「未关闭」的日耳曼语形容词加英语副词后缀 -ly 构成；它周围的一族词再用名词形式表示缺口、动作与性质。

latinIntro.en: Open is native English and Germanic, and no reliable Latin cognate is recorded for it.
latinIntro.cn: open 属英语本土的日耳曼词，这个词没有可靠的拉丁同族词记录。

scene: 假期最后一晚，一家人换上正式衣服，走进河边那座老剧场，准备从头听到尾。The whole family dressed up to hear an opera that lasted four hours.

直接来自拉丁语 opus（作品），与 opera 同出一源，义为「作品；乐曲」

senses.title: A drama sung on stage
senses.definition: a play set to music, in which the story is told through singing rather than ordinary speech
senses.definitionCN: 谱成音乐的戏剧，故事用歌唱而不是日常说话来讲
senses.example: The new opera was written by a young composer.
senses.exampleCN: 这部新歌剧由一位年轻作曲家写成。
senses.why: Latin opera is the plural of opus, a work; Italian took it for a musical work, and English borrowed that name for the kind of drama that is sung.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 opera 是 opus（作品）的复数；意大利语借它指「谱成音乐的作品」，英语再借来，就成了这类唱着演的戏剧的名字。

senses.title: The art form itself
senses.titleCN: 歌剧艺术；歌剧这一体裁
senses.definition: the art form or genre of such works, considered as a whole
senses.definitionCN: 把这类作品作为整体来看的艺术形式或门类
senses.example: She has spent thirty years in opera.
senses.exampleCN: 她在歌剧这一行干了三十年。
senses.why: Once it names individual works, the word can name the whole field those works belong to, just as a kind of object can give its name to a craft.
senses.whyCN: 既然能指一部部作品，也就能指这些作品所属的整个领域；就像某类物件可以给出一个行当的名字。

senses.title: The building or the company
senses.definition: the theatre, or the company, where such works are staged
senses.definitionCN: 上演这类作品的剧院，或经营它的团体
senses.example: The opera is rebuilding its stage this winter.
senses.exampleCN: 歌剧院今年冬天要重修它的舞台。
senses.why: A place or an institution often takes the name of the art it presents, so the word moves from the work to the house that performs it.
senses.whyCN: 演出场所或团体常直接拿它所演的艺术来命名，词义就从「作品」转到「上演作品的房子」。

intro.en: Opera reached English through Italian, but behind it sits the Latin word for a work; its family includes opus and operatic, not the separate verb for working.
intro.cn: opera 经意大利语进入英语，背后却是拉丁语中「作品」这个词；同族词包括 opus 与 operatic，而不包括另一个表示「干活」的动词。

items.en: Latin opus meant work, effort or a product, and its plural opera meant works; the genitive operis keeps the same stem.
items.cn: 拉丁语 opus 指工作、出力或成果，复数 opera 指多件作品；属格 operis 保留同一词干。

items.en: In Latin, opera could already name a work of art, and the phrase opera in musica named a work set to music.
items.cn: 在拉丁语中 opera 已经可以指一件艺术品，短语 opera in musica 专指「谱成音乐的作品」。

items.en: Italian composers and audiences made opera the name of the new sung drama, and that sense became fixed.
items.cn: 十七世纪的意大利作曲家与观众拿 opera 当作这种新的歌唱戏剧的名字，词义就此固定下来。

items.en: English borrowed the Italian word and soon used it for the building where such works were staged, giving opera house.
items.cn: 英语借入这个意大利词，很快又用它指上演这类作品的建筑，于是有了 opera house。

items.en: Modern English keeps the musical sense and loosens it in soap opera, where the link is serial drama rather than song.
items.cn: 现代英语保留音乐戏剧的含义，并在 soap opera 里把这种联系放宽到长篇连续剧，与歌唱无关。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers the Latin words for a work and the operatic family; the near-meaning group gathers other staged or sung arts.
note.cn: 形近组收与「作品」有关、来自拉丁语的同族词；近义组收其他舞台或声乐艺术。

entries.definitionCN: 与歌剧有关的，或像歌剧那样夸张的。

entries.definitionCN: 艺术作品，尤指音乐作品。

entries.definitionCN: 有对白与唱段的短小轻歌剧。

entries.definition: A comic opera in the Italian tradition.
entries.definitionCN: 意大利传统中的喜歌剧。

entries.definition: A stage show that mixes songs, dance and spoken scenes.
entries.definitionCN: 把歌曲、舞蹈与对白场面混合的舞台演出。

entries.definition: A long musical work on a sacred subject, sung without staging.
entries.definitionCN: 以宗教题材写成、只唱不演的长篇音乐作品。

entries.definition: A staged dance work with music but without singing.
entries.definitionCN: 有音乐、无歌唱的舞台舞蹈作品。

normalIntro.en: Opera is a Latin plural that Italian turned into the name of a sung play, and the family keeps circling the idea of a work.
normalIntro.cn: opera 本是拉丁语的复数形式，意大利语把它变成一路唱着演的戏剧之名；这一族词都绕着「作品」打转。

normal.en: Opera is the plural of opus, so the word literally means works.
normal.cn: opera 是 opus 的复数，字面上就是「多件作品」。

normal.en: The Latin phrase opera in musica is the seed of the modern sense: a work set to music.
normal.cn: 拉丁短语 opera in musica 是现代词义的种子：谱上音乐的「作品」。

normal.en: Opera house names the building after the art, a common pattern for theatres.
normal.cn: opera house 用艺术之名来命名建筑，这是剧院常见的命名方式。

normal.en: Operatic adds -ic, meaning belonging to opera or behaving like someone on its stage.
normal.cn: operatic 加 -ic，意为属于歌剧的，或像站在歌剧舞台上那样夸张。

normal.en: Operetta is a small opera, because the Italian diminutive makes the genre light and short.
normal.cn: operetta 是「小歌剧」，意大利语的指小形式让这个门类变得轻巧短小。

abstract.en: One word for works, a genre and a building shows how a single name can shelter a whole art.
abstract.cn: 一个词同时指作品、门类和建筑，说明一个名字可以把一门艺术整个罩住。

abstract.en: The audience sits in the dark while a story is carried entirely by the human voice.
abstract.cn: 观众坐进黑暗里，整个故事只靠人声扛着走。

abstract.en: Singing turns ordinary speech into something too large for a living room.
abstract.cn: 歌唱把日常说话放大成客厅装不下的东西。

examples.en: The new opera was written by a young composer.
examples.cn: 这部新歌剧由一位年轻作曲家写成。

examples.en: She has spent thirty years in opera.

root: 拉丁语 opus（工作、成果，属格 operis）的复数 opera 意为「作品」，意大利语用它指「谱成音乐的戏剧」，十七世纪传入英语。它与 operate 不是同一个词：operate 来自拉丁动词 operari（干活、起作用），两条路线不同，现代英语里不能互换。

sensesIntro.en: The core is a work set to music; the senses divide into one staged work, the art form as a whole, and the house or company that presents it.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是「谱成音乐的成品」；义项分为一部具体的舞台作品、作为整体的艺术门类，以及上演它的场所或团体。

branches.cn: 年轻作曲家深夜写完一部总谱

branches.en: the curtain falling after the last aria
branches.cn: 最后一段咏叹调唱完，幕布落下

branches.en: a singer choosing a life on the stage
branches.cn: 歌唱者选择以舞台为业

branches.cn: 剧团把布景装上卡车去巡演

intro.en: The word rests on a Latin plural for works, passes through Italian, and gathers English compounds for the house, the singer and the company.
intro.cn: 这个词建立在拉丁语表示「作品」的复数形式上，经意大利语中转，再在英语里聚起一批指剧院、演员和剧团的复合词。

latinIntro.en: The Latin family behind opera is the opus family: a work, its plural, and the adjectives built on them.
latinIntro.cn: opera 背后的拉丁词族是 opus 一族：作品、它的复数，以及由它们构成的形容词。

definition_zh: 操作；运转；经营；动手术
definition_en: to work or function, to control a machine, to run a business, or to perform a medical operation
core_image: 一只手按下按钮，整排机器依次发出低响，像身体里某处重新开始供血
scene: 深夜的泵房里，值班员按下启动键，旧水泵先抖了两下，随后平稳地响了起来。The old pump began to operate smoothly after the valve was replaced.
sceneCN: 这里是「运转」（第 1 个义项：机器或系统开始工作并保持运行）；句意为换过阀门之后，旧水泵开始平稳运转。图中可辨识物件：泵房管道、启动键、压力表。

senses.title: To work or run
senses.definition: to work or function, especially of a machine, system or service
senses.definitionCN: 尤指机器、系统或服务在工作、起作用
senses.example: The heating system operates at low cost in winter.
senses.exampleCN: 这套供暖系统冬天运行成本很低。
senses.why: Latin operari means to work, so a machine that runs is the old idea of working moved from a person onto a device.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 operari 意为「干活」，机器在运行这个义项，就是把「干活」从人身上挪到了装置上。

senses.title: To control a machine
senses.definition: to control or use a machine, vehicle or piece of equipment
senses.definitionCN: 控制并使用机器、车辆或设备
senses.example: Only trained staff may operate the crane.
senses.exampleCN: 只有受过训练的人员才能操作这台起重机。
senses.why: If a machine can work by itself, a person can also make it work, and the transitive use simply adds a hand on the controls.
senses.whyCN: 机器既然能自己运行，人也能使它运行；及物用法只是在「干活」这件事上多了一只放在操纵杆上的手。

senses.title: To perform surgery
senses.definition: to cut into a patient's body in order to treat a disease or an injury
senses.definitionCN: 切开病人身体以治疗疾病或损伤
senses.example: Surgeons operated on her knee at dawn.
senses.exampleCN: 外科医生在黎明时为她做了膝关节手术。
senses.why: Surgery is skilled work done with the hands on the body, so the general verb for working took the medical sense through the phrase operate on.
senses.whyCN: 手术是靠双手在身体上完成的技艺活，于是「干活」这个泛用动词借着 operate on 这个说法，担起了医学含义。

senses.title: To run a business or organization
senses.definition: to manage or run a business, service or organization
senses.definitionCN: 管理或经营一项生意、服务或组织
senses.example: The charity operates three shelters in the city.
senses.exampleCN: 这家慈善机构在市内经营三家收容所。
senses.why: Running an organization is continuous work, so the same verb moves from a single machine to a whole enterprise.
senses.whyCN: 经营一个组织是持续不断的活，同一个动词就这样从一台机器扩大到整个机构。

intro.en: Operate comes straight from Latin, where a verb for working gave English both the verb and its nouns; it is not the same word as opera, which arrived through Italian.
intro.cn: operate 直接从拉丁语进入英语，那里一个意为「干活」的动词为英语提供了动词和它的名词；它与经意大利语而来的 opera 不是同一个词。

items.en: Latin opus named work or a product, and its genitive operis supplied the stem for the verbs of working.
items.cn: 拉丁语 opus 指工作或成果，属格 operis 为表示「干活」的一系列动词提供了词干。

items.en: Operari was a deponent verb meaning to work, to labor or to produce an effect.
items.cn: operari 是一个异态动词，意为干活、劳作或产生作用。

items.en: Its past participle operatus meant having worked, and this is the form English took when it borrowed the verb.
items.cn: 它的过去分词 operatus 意为「已经干过」，英语借入动词时带的就是这个形式。

items.en: Early English operate meant to produce an effect or to exert force, a sense still heard in the word operation.
items.cn: 早期的英语 operate 意为产生效果或施加力量，这层意思至今还能在 operation 里听到。

items.en: Modern English widened operate to machines, businesses and surgery while keeping the older sense of having an effect.
items.cn: 现代英语把 operate 扩展到机器、企业和手术，同时保留了「起作用」这层旧义。

note.en: The look-alike group is the Latin-derived working family; the near-meaning group is everyday verbs for running or handling something.
note.cn: 形近组是由拉丁语「干活」长出的词族；近义组是日常里表示运转或摆弄某物的动词。

entries.definition: The act of working, or a medical procedure.
entries.definitionCN: 运作的行为，或医疗手术。

entries.definition: Working, or used for working, as in an operating system.
entries.definitionCN: 运转的或用于运转的，如操作系统。

entries.definition: A person who works a machine or handles telephone calls.
entries.definitionCN: 操作机器或处理电话的人。

entries.definition: Working or in force, and also a person who carries out secret work.
entries.definitionCN: 起作用的、实施中的，也指从事秘密工作的人。

entries.definition: To make a machine or a business work.
entries.definitionCN: 使机器或企业运转。

entries.definition: To work in the normal or expected way.
entries.definitionCN: 以正常或预期的方式工作。

entries.definition: To use or control something with the hands.
entries.definitionCN: 用手使用或控制某物。

normalIntro.en: Everything in this family goes back to the Latin verb for working, so the mnemonics follow the work from hands to machines to bodies.
normalIntro.cn: 这一族词都可追到拉丁语表示「干活」的动词，所以联想沿着「活」从双手走到机器，再到身体。

normal.en: Operari means to work, so operate is first of all to be busy doing something.
normal.cn: operari 意为干活，所以 operate 首先是「在忙着做某事」。

normal.en: Operation adds -tion and turns the working into a thing you can name.
normal.cn: operation 加 -tion，把「干活」变成一个可以叫出名字的东西。

normal.en: Operator adds -or and turns the working into the person who does it.
normal.cn: operator 加 -or，把「干活」变成干活的那个人。

normal.en: Operate on is the medical phrase, where the body is the thing being worked on.
normal.cn: operate on 是医学说法，被「干活」的对象就是身体。

normal.en: Operative means still at work, which is why a spy is also called one.
normal.cn: operative 意为仍在起作用，这就是特工也被叫作 operative 的原因。

abstract.en: A hand on a lever is the shortest picture of operate: effort passing into a machine.
abstract.cn: 一只手搭在操纵杆上，就是 operate 最短的画面：力气传进机器。

abstract.en: A machine that runs is a person's work continuing after the person has stepped away.
abstract.cn: 机器自己转着，就是人的活在离开之后还继续着。

abstract.en: Cutting a body to mend it shows how far the plain word for working can travel.
abstract.cn: 切开身体去修补它，说明「干活」这个平常词能走多远。

examples.en: The old pump began to operate smoothly after the valve was replaced.
examples.cn: 换过阀门之后，旧水泵开始平稳运转。

examples.en: Only trained staff may operate the crane.
examples.cn: 只有受过训练的人员才能操作这台起重机。

examples.en: The charity operates three shelters in the city.
examples.cn: 这家慈善机构在市内经营三家收容所。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「哦，怕累他」——机器开动以后，最怕累坏那个守着它的人；记住 operate 是操作、运转。

root: 拉丁语 opus（工作、成果）派生动词 operari（干活、起作用），过去分词 operatus 进入英语成为 operate；同族词有 operation、operator、operative、operating。opera 虽与它共享更远的拉丁词根，却经意大利语而来、指「歌剧」，不能与 operate 混用。

sensesIntro.en: The core is work being done; the senses move from a machine running, to a hand controlling it, to surgery, and finally to running a whole enterprise.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是「正在干的活」；义项从机器自己运行，移到人伸手操纵，再到在身体上动刀，最后到经营整个机构。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a hand pressing a button and a row of machines answering with a low hum.
core.cn: 核心意象：一只手按下按钮，一排机器用低沉的声音回应。

branches.cn: 修好之后水泵重新找到节奏

branches.en: an operator guiding a crane over a roof
branches.cn: 操作员把起重机吊过屋顶

branches.cn: 学徒练习让两只手保持不动

senses.title: The working of a machine or system
senses.definition: the way in which a device, plant or system performs its function
senses.definitionCN: 装置、工厂或系统发挥功能的方式
senses.example: The pump's operation is monitored from a control room.
senses.exampleCN: 泵的运转由控制室监控。
senses.why: The word rests on a Latin verb meaning to work, so the working of a system is its most literal sense.
senses.whyCN: 这个词建立在拉丁语「工作」动词之上，因此系统的运转是它最字面的义项。

senses.title: The act of making a device work
senses.definition: the act of running or controlling a machine by hand or by control
senses.definitionCN: 用手或控制装置使机器运行的动作
senses.example: Operation of the crane requires two trained hands.
senses.exampleCN: 操作这台吊车需要两名受过训练的人。
senses.why: Doing the work and making something else work are two sides of one verb, so the act of driving a machine took the same noun.
senses.whyCN: 自己干活与让别的东西干活是同一个动词的两面，因此驱动机器的动作也用了这个名词。

senses.title: A surgical treatment
senses.definition: a treatment in which a surgeon cuts into or enters the body to repair it
senses.definitionCN: 外科医生切开或进入体内进行修补的治疗
senses.example: The operation on her knee lasted two hours.
senses.exampleCN: 她膝盖的手术持续了两个小时。
senses.why: Surgery is work done on a body, so medicine used the general noun for work and it became the everyday word for an intervention.
senses.whyCN: 手术是对身体所做的工作，因此医学用这个泛指「工作」的名词，它后来成了介入治疗的日常说法。

senses.title: A planned military action
senses.definition: an organized movement of forces with a set aim, usually given a name
senses.definitionCN: 有明确目标、通常有代号的部队组织行动
senses.example: The rescue operation began at dawn.
senses.exampleCN: 救援行动在黎明开始。
senses.why: Military staffs speak of work done by combined forces as one operation, and the sense spread to any coordinated action.
senses.whyCN: 军事参谋把多支部队合力完成的工作称为一次行动，这个义项后来扩展到任何协同行动。

senses.title: The everyday activities of a business
senses.definition: the routine activities by which a company or institution keeps running, usually in the plural
senses.definitionCN: 公司或机构维持运转的日常活动，常用复数
senses.example: The firm moved its operations closer to the port.
senses.exampleCN: 这家公司把业务迁到离港口更近的地方。
senses.why: A business is a set of workings, so its routine activities are called its operations rather than its plans.
senses.whyCN: 一家企业就是一组运转，因此它的日常活动被称为业务，而不是计划。

senses.title: A mathematical process
senses.definition: a rule applied to numbers or symbols to produce a new value
senses.definitionCN: 施于数字或符号以得出新值的规则
senses.example: Addition is the first operation children learn.
senses.exampleCN: 加法是孩子学的第一种运算。
senses.why: Mathematics treats each rule as work performed on symbols, which is the same idea of a working applied to numbers.
senses.whyCN: 数学把每条规则看作对符号所做的工作，这与「运转」是同一个意思，只是对象换成数字。

senses.title: A running business or unit
senses.definition: an enterprise or a distinct unit that is being run as a going concern
senses.definitionCN: 作为持续经营体运作的企业或独立单位
senses.example: The mine is a profitable operation.
senses.exampleCN: 这座矿是一个盈利的经营单位。
senses.why: Once a business is seen as something that works, the thing that works can itself be called an operation.
senses.whyCN: 一旦企业被看作在运转的东西，这个在运转的东西本身就可以被称为一个经营单位。

senses.title: An organized piece of work with a plan
senses.titleCN: 有组织的行动；专项行动
senses.definition: a coordinated piece of work, often large, carried out by a group toward one aim
senses.definitionCN: 由一群人朝同一目标实施的、常具规模的协同工作
senses.example: The cleanup operation involved three hundred volunteers.
senses.exampleCN: 这次清理行动动用了三百名志愿者。
senses.why: Any large piece of coordinated work can be called an operation, because it is work organized as one working whole.
senses.whyCN: 任何大规模协同工作都可称为一次行动，因为它被组织成一个整体的运作。

intro.en: Operation came through Old French from Latin operatio 'a working', built on operari 'to work' and opus 'work'. The origin of opus before Latin is unsettled. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: 这个词经古法语来自拉丁语表示「工作」的名词，其基础为表示「工作」的动词与名词。名词词根在拉丁语之前的来源没有定论。年代均为约数。

items.en: Opus meant 'work, a piece of work, a task'. Its pre-Latin origin is not established, and the root sometimes proposed for it is a reconstruction, so source uncertain at that depth.
items.cn: opus 意为「工作、一件作品、任务」。其在拉丁语之前的来源未获证明，有时为它提出的词根属重构形式，故更深一层来源不确定。

items.en: Operari, a deponent verb, meant 'to work, to labour, to perform'.
items.cn: operari 是一个异态动词，意为「工作、劳作、施行」。

items.en: Operatio, from operari plus the noun suffix -io, named a working or the result of working.
items.cn: operatio 由 operari 加名词后缀 -io 构成，指工作这一动作或其结果。

items.en: Old French brought the noun into English in the fourteenth century, first for any action or effect.
items.cn: 古法语在十四世纪把这个名词带入英语，最初指任何动作或效果。

items.en: From the seventeenth century surgery adopted the word for an intervention, and from the eighteenth military staffs used it for a named action.
items.cn: 十七世纪起外科把这个词用于介入治疗，十八世纪起军事参谋用它指有代号的行动。

note.en: Group one holds words built on the same Latin noun of work, plus one that only looks similar; group two holds words that overlap with it in meaning.
note.cn: 第一组是同出拉丁「工作」名词的词，外加一个仅形似的词；第二组是语义上与本词重叠的词。

entries.definition: To run a machine, to carry on business or to perform surgery; the noun names the working, the verb performs it.
entries.definitionCN: 指运转机器、开展业务或施行手术；名词指运转本身，动词指施行。

entries.definition: The person who runs a machine or a business, formed with the agent suffix.
entries.definitionCN: 用施动后缀构成，指操作机器或经营业务的人。

entries.definition: Co- 'together' plus the same verb: joint work, with no single unit of action.
entries.definitionCN: co-「共同」加同一动词：指共同工作，不指单个动作单元。

entries.definition: From orare 'to speak', not from opus: a formal speech, similar only in its ending.
entries.definitionCN: 出自 orare「说话」，而非 opus：指正式演说，仅词尾相似。

entries.definition: The branch of medicine and the procedure itself, with nothing about machines or business.
entries.definitionCN: 指外科这一学科及手术本身，与机器或业务无关。

entries.definition: The ordered steps of an action; it does not imply that anything is actually running.
entries.definitionCN: 指行动的有序步骤，并不表示事情真的在运转。

entries.definition: The proper role or capacity of a part; it names what something is for, not how it runs.
entries.definitionCN: 指某部件的应有作用或能力，说明它用于什么，而非如何运转。

entries.definition: A connected series of actions for one aim, often public or military; it stresses duration, not a single working.
entries.definitionCN: 为同一目标展开的系列行动，常为宣传或军事行动；强调持续时间，而非单次运作。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: A Latin noun of work plus a noun suffix: the doing of work, and then any piece of work that is done.
normal.cn: 拉丁「工作」名词加名词后缀：先指干活，再指所干的任一件事。

normal.en: One root yields the verb to run, the person who runs, the adjective for running order and the noun for joint work.
normal.cn: 同一词根给出表示运转的动词、表示操作者的名词、表示运转状态的形容词，以及表示合作的名词。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the settings: in operation, surgical operation, rescue operation, daily operations.
normal.cn: 固定说法标出场景：在运转中、外科手术、救援行动、日常业务。

normal.en: Hospitals, armies and mathematics all call their own kind of work by this one name.
normal.cn: 医院、军队与数学都把自己那类工作用同一个名称来称呼。

normal.en: A factory is said to be in operation, and later the factory itself is called an operation.
normal.cn: 工厂被说成处于运转中，后来工厂本身也被称为一个经营单位。

abstract.en: Picture a clock whose gears keep turning while nobody watches.
abstract.cn: 想象一座钟的齿轮在无人注视时仍不停转动。

abstract.en: Picture a surgeon's hands as the only still thing in a room full of machines.
abstract.cn: 想象一屋子机器都在动，只有外科医生的手是静的。

abstract.en: Picture a column of figures that changes when one rule is applied.
abstract.cn: 想象一列数字在施加一条规则后整体改变。

examples.en: The plant has been in operation since the river was dammed.
examples.cn: 这座工厂自河流筑坝以来一直在运转。

examples.en: The peacekeeping operation was extended for another six months.
examples.cn: 维和行动又延长了六个月。

examples.en: Division is the operation most often done wrong under time pressure.
examples.cn: 除法是时间紧迫时最容易算错的一种运算。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「oper（工作）+ ation（名词）」——在工作、在运转 → 运转、操作、手术、行动、运算

root: 拉丁语「工作」名词派生出「工作、施行」的动词，再加后缀构成「工作、运作」的名词；名词词根更早的来源无定论，相关词根属重构形式。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one act of working: a machine runs, a hand makes it run, a surgeon works on a body, an army works on an objective, a company works every day, a rule works on numbers, a working enterprise is itself a unit, and any coordinated effort is one operation.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿同一个「工作」动作展开：机器运转、手使它运转、医生在身体上工作、军队对一个目标行动、公司每天运作、规则对数字起作用、运转中的企业本身成为一个单位，最后任何协同用力都算一次行动。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: gears turning under a lamp while a hand rests on the switch that keeps them turning.
core.cn: 核心意象：灯下齿轮转动，一只手按在使它们继续转动的开关上。

branches.en: RUNNING AND DRIVING: the working of a system and the act that keeps it working are one event seen from two sides.
branches.cn: 运转与驱动：系统的运转与使它运转的动作，是同一件事的两面。

branches.en: ON A BODY: surgery is work performed on flesh with tools.
branches.cn: 施于身体：手术是用工具在血肉上所做的工作。

branches.en: ON AN AIM: a named military action and any coordinated effort are work organized toward one end.
branches.cn: 对准目标：有代号的军事行动与任何协同工作，都是朝一个目标组织起来的劳动。

branches.en: THE WORKING UNIT: a company's daily business and the enterprise itself are the same working seen as activity and as thing.
branches.cn: 运转单位：公司的日常业务与企业本身，是同一个运转被看作活动与看作实体。

branches.en: ON SYMBOLS: arithmetic applies the same notion of work to numbers.
branches.cn: 施于符号：算术把同一个「工作」观念用在数字上。

intro.en: Operation is a Latin noun of work: a root noun for a task and a verb for doing it, with a suffix that turns the doing into a name.
intro.cn: 这是一个表示「工作」的拉丁名词：一个指任务的词根名词、一个指做这件事的动词，以及把「做」变成名称的后缀。

latinIntro.en: Latin opus and operari give operate, operator, operation and cooperation; the noun suffix marks the act or its result.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语中表示「工作」的名词与动词衍生出运转、操作者与合作等词；名词后缀标记动作或其结果。

items.example: The root noun names the task itself.
items.exampleCN: 这个词根名词指任务本身。

items.example: The verb turns the task into activity.
items.exampleCN: 这个动词把任务变成活动。

items.example: The suffix makes the activity a countable thing.
items.exampleCN: 后缀把活动变成可计数的东西。

items.example: English keeps both the activity and its result.
items.exampleCN: 英语兼指动作与其结果。

items.example: The suffix is the same one that builds many nouns of process.
items.exampleCN: 这个后缀也构成许多表示过程的名词。

items.example: One verb covers machines, businesses and surgeons.
items.exampleCN: 一个动词兼指机器、企业与外科医生。

items.meaning: one who works a machine or business
items.meaningCN: 操作机器或经营业务的人
items.example: The agent suffix names the person at the controls.
items.exampleCN: 施动后缀指在控制台前的人。

items.example: The prefix makes the work shared.
items.exampleCN: 前缀使这份工作成为共享的。

items.meaningCN: 处于运转状态的；生效的
items.example: A rule becomes operative when it starts to apply.
items.exampleCN: 规则开始适用时便生效。

sceneCN: 这里 operational 是“已具备运行条件、可投入使用”（第 2 个义项）；句意：系统下周就可以投入运行；对应第 1 个义项。

senses.title: Relating to how it runs
senses.titleCN: 运行上的：与机器怎么转有关
senses.definition: relating to the working of a machine, system, or process
senses.definitionCN: 与机器、系统或流程如何运转有关
senses.example: The engineers separated design problems from operational problems.
senses.exampleCN: 工程师把设计问题与运行问题分开处理。
senses.why: The suffix -al points to a domain: what happens while the thing is running, as distinct from how it was designed.
senses.whyCN: 后缀 -al 指向一个领域：事物运转时发生的事，与它如何被设计区分开来。

senses.title: Ready to be used
senses.titleCN: 可投入使用：不是图纸，是能跑的
senses.definition: in a state of being able to work or be used as intended
senses.definitionCN: 处于能够按预期工作或使用的状态
senses.example: The new control tower is operational after two years of testing.
senses.exampleCN: 新控制塔经过两年测试后已可投入使用。
senses.why: Here the word answers a readiness question: the thing is not merely complete on paper, it can actually perform its function.
senses.whyCN: 这里这个词回答的是“就绪”问题：事物不只在纸面上完成，它真能履行职责。

senses.title: The cost of keeping it running
senses.titleCN: 运营成本：让它每天转起来的钱
senses.definition: describing the expenses of running an organization or facility rather than building it
senses.definitionCN: 指维持组织或设施日常运转的开支，而非建设开支
senses.example: Operational costs rose with fuel and staff wages.
senses.exampleCN: 运营成本随燃料与员工工资上涨。
senses.why: Budgets split capital from operation: one pays to build, the other pays to keep the thing alive each day.
senses.whyCN: 预算把资本支出与运营支出分开：一笔付建设，另一笔付让它每天活下去。

senses.title: Defined by what you do
senses.titleCN: 操作定义：用做法代替概念
senses.definition: describing a definition that specifies the procedures or measurements used to identify something
senses.definitionCN: 指用识别某事物所需的具体程序或测量来下定义
senses.example: The study operationalised 'stress' as a rise in heart rate during the task.
senses.exampleCN: 该研究把“压力”操作化为任务期间心率上升。
senses.why: Some ideas cannot be seen directly, so science defines them by the operations that produce them, making the concept testable.
senses.whyCN: 有些概念无法直接看见，科学便用产生它的操作来定义，使概念可被检验。

senses.title: The mathematics of decisions
senses.titleCN: 运筹：把调度问题算清楚
senses.definition: describing the use of mathematical methods to improve the planning and running of complex activities
senses.definitionCN: 指用数学方法改进复杂活动的计划与运行
senses.example: Operational research cut the average waiting time at the depot.
senses.exampleCN: 运筹研究缩短了车站的平均等待时间。
senses.why: When an organization runs, its choices can be modelled; operational research treats scheduling as a problem with a best answer.
senses.whyCN: 组织一旦运转，其选择就可以建模型；运筹研究把调度当作一个有最优解的问题。

senses.title: At the level of action
senses.titleCN: 作战层面：战略之下、战术之上
senses.definition: describing the level of military activity concerned with planning and conducting campaigns
senses.definitionCN: 指军事活动中负责筹划与实施战役的层级
senses.example: Operational command decided where the units would meet before the battle.
senses.exampleCN: 作战指挥决定各部队在战斗前于何处会合。
senses.why: Military theory separates strategy (why to fight), operations (where and when to move), and tactics (how to fight the next hour).
senses.whyCN: 军事理论把战略（为何打）、作战（何时何地调动）与战术（接下来一小时怎么打）分开。

senses.title: Risk from daily running
senses.titleCN: 运营风险：不是市场，而是流程出错
senses.definition: describing the risk of loss from failed processes, people, systems, or external events
senses.definitionCN: 指因流程、人员、系统失效或外部事件造成损失的风险
senses.example: The bank holds capital against operational risk as well as credit risk.
senses.exampleCN: 银行不仅为信用风险，也为运营风险持有资本。
senses.why: Finance distinguishes risk from markets and borrowers from risk that arises simply because an organization must run every day.
senses.whyCN: 金融业把市场与借款人的风险，同“组织每天必须运转”本身带来的风险区分开。

senses.title: A circuit that computes
senses.titleCN: 运算放大器：让电路做算术
senses.definition: describing an amplifier designed to perform mathematical operations on signals
senses.definitionCN: 指为对信号执行数学运算而设计的放大器
senses.example: The operational amplifier summed the two sensor voltages.
senses.exampleCN: 运算放大器把两个传感器的电压相加。
senses.why: Early analogue computers used amplifiers to add and integrate; the name stayed even after the circuits became general-purpose components.
senses.whyCN: 早期模拟计算机用放大器做加法与积分；即使这些电路后来成了通用元件，名字仍保留下来。

intro.en: Operational is operation plus -al. Operation comes from Latin operatio, a working, from operari, to work, and opus, work.
intro.cn: operational 是 operation 加 -al。operation 来自拉丁语 operatio“劳作”，出自 operari“工作”与 opus“工作、作品”。

items.en: Opus meant work, a task, or a product of work. It survives in magnum opus and in the musical term opera.
items.cn: opus 意为工作、任务或劳动成果。它留在 magnum opus 与音乐术语 opera 中。

items.en: The verb meant to work, to labour, and to perform a task. It could describe both physical labour and the working of a power.
items.cn: 该动词意为工作、劳作、执行任务，既可描述体力劳动，也可描述某种力量的作用。

items.en: The noun named a working or an effect produced. Medieval Latin also used it for mathematical and medical procedures.
items.cn: 该名词指劳作或产生的效果。中世纪拉丁语也用它指数学与医学操作。

items.en: French operation covered work, a surgical procedure, and a military action. English borrowed all three.
items.cn: 法语 operation 涵盖工作、外科手术与军事行动；英语把这三层都借了进来。

items.en: Operational first meant 'of an operation' in surgery and mathematics, then extended to machines and organizations in the industrial age.
items.cn: operational 最初指外科与数学意义上的“操作的”， industrial 时代扩展到机器与组织。

items.en: The 20th century added operational research, operational definition, operational risk, and the operational amplifier.
items.cn: 20 世纪增加了运筹研究、操作定义、运营风险与运算放大器等用法。

note.en: The first group is the operate family; the second compares adjectives that describe readiness, function, and practical work.
note.cn: 第一组是 operate 词族；第二组比较表示就绪、功能与实际运作的形容词。

entries.definition: to work or control a machine, to run a business, or to perform surgery.
entries.definitionCN: 操作或控制机器、经营业务，或施行手术。

entries.definition: the act of working, a surgical procedure, or a military action.
entries.definitionCN: 工作行为、外科手术，或军事行动。

entries.definition: a person who runs a machine, or a company that runs a service.
entries.definitionCN: 操作机器的人，或经营某项服务的公司。

entries.definition: working as designed. It stresses purpose served, while operational can also stress the running process or its cost.
entries.definitionCN: 按设计正常工作；强调所服务的目的，而 operational 也可强调运行过程或成本。

entries.definition: useful in real situations rather than theoretical. It judges usefulness, not running status.
entries.definitionCN: 在真实情境中有用而非理论的；判断的是用处，不是运行状态。

entries.definition: in action or in effect. A system can be active without being fully operational.
entries.definitionCN: 正在行动或生效的；系统可以处于活动状态却尚未完全可运行。

entries.definition: relating to long-term aims. In military theory it is the level above operational.
entries.definitionCN: 与长期目标有关；在军事理论中位于“作战”之上。

normalIntro.en: Real parts only: opus, work, plus operari, to work, then -ation and -al. Operational means 'of the working'.
normalIntro.cn: 只用真实成分：opus“工作”，加 operari“工作”，再加 -ation 与 -al。operational 就是“属于运转的”。

normal.en: Opus is work; operational is the adjective of work being done right now.
normal.cn: opus 是工作；operational 是“工作正在进行”的形容词。

normal.en: Design is the drawing; operational is the machine actually turning.
normal.cn: 设计是图纸；operational 是机器真的在转。

normal.en: Operational costs are the money paid every day, not the money paid to build.
normal.cn: 运营成本是每天都要付的钱，不是建造时付的钱。

normal.en: An operational definition says what you do, not what you mean.
normal.cn: 操作定义说的是你怎么做，而不是你指什么。

normal.en: All green lights mean the system is operational.
normal.cn: 指示灯全绿，就表示系统处于可运行状态。

abstract.en: 'Operational' is where plans meet friction: everything works on paper, and only some things work at three in the morning.
abstract.cn: operational 是计划撞上摩擦的地方：纸面上一切都能行，凌晨三点只有一部分真能行。

abstract.en: An operational definition trades depth for testability, and the trade is usually worth making.
abstract.cn: 操作定义用深度换可检验性，这笔交易通常值得。

abstract.en: The word hides the labour inside the system; what looks automatic is a schedule of people and maintenance.
abstract.cn: 这个词把系统里的劳动藏了起来；看似自动的东西，其实是一张排班表与维护表。

examples.en: The plant became fully operational only after the cooling system passed its safety test.
examples.cn: 冷却系统通过安全测试后，这座工厂才全面投入运行。

examples.en: Operational costs, not construction costs, decide whether the railway survives.
examples.cn: 决定这条铁路能否存续的是运营成本，而不是建设成本。

examples.en: The team agreed on an operational definition of 'success' before collecting any data.
examples.cn: 团队在收集数据之前先就“成功”的操作定义达成一致。

dict_mnemonic.text: operate（运行）+ ional（的）——能跑起来、正在运转的，都是 operational。

root: 由 operation（运行、操作，源自拉丁语 operatio“劳作”）加 -al 构成；词基为拉丁语 opus“工作”与 operari“工作”，故本义为“与运转、操作有关的”。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses of operational, all concerned with work being done. The work may be a machine turning, a system ready to run, the cost of daily upkeep, a procedure that defines a concept, a mathematical plan, a military campaign, a process failure, or an analogue computation.
sensesIntro.cn: operational 的八个义项都与“正在做的工作”有关。这工作可以是机器转动、系统就绪、日常维护成本、定义概念的程序、数学调度、军事战役、流程失效，或模拟电路运算。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a production line running with every indicator green and nobody waiting for a repair.
core.cn: 核心意象：生产线正在运转，指示灯全绿，没有人等着维修。

chain: ENGLISH OPERATION THE ACT OF RUNNING
OPERATIONAL OF RUNNING OR READY TO RUN

branches.en: RUNNING AND READY: the process of working, and the state of being fit to work.
branches.cn: 运转与就绪：工作的过程，以及能够工作的状态。

branches.en: THE PRICE OF RUNNING: daily costs and the risks that arise from ordinary processes.
branches.cn: 运转的代价：日常成本，以及普通流程带来的风险。

branches.en: DEFINITION BY PROCEDURE: a concept replaced by the operations that measure it.
branches.cn: 以程序定义：用测量它的操作取代概念本身。

branches.en: PLANNING ACTION: mathematical scheduling and the military level between strategy and tactics.
branches.cn: 筹划行动：数学调度，以及位于战略与战术之间的军事层级。

branches.en: COMPUTING BY CIRCUIT: an amplifier named for the operations it performs.
branches.cn: 用电路运算：因执行运算而得名的放大器。

intro.en: Operational is operation plus -al. The family runs through operate, operator, and operation, with opus as the Latin base.
intro.cn: operational 是 operation 加 -al。词族包括 operate、operator、operation，拉丁词基为 opus。

latinIntro.en: The base is opus, work, and its verb operari. Latin operatio names the working or the effect produced.
latinIntro.cn: 词基是 opus“工作”及其动词 operari。拉丁语 operatio 指劳作或产生的效果。

items.meaning: to work, control, or carry out an activity
items.example: Only trained staff may operate the crane.
items.exampleCN: 只有受过训练的员工可以操作这台起重机。

items.meaning: the act of working, or a planned action
items.meaningCN: 工作行为，或计划好的行动
items.example: The operation runs from six in the morning.
items.exampleCN: 这项作业从早晨六点开始运行。

items.meaning: relating to running, or ready to run
items.meaningCN: 与运行有关的，或已可运行的
items.example: The system is operational but not yet open to the public.
items.exampleCN: 系统已可运行，但尚未向公众开放。

items.meaning: from the point of view of running
items.example: Operationally, the two designs are almost the same.
items.exampleCN: 从运行角度看，两种设计几乎一样。

items.meaning: a person or firm that runs something
items.meaningCN: 操作者，或经营某项业务的公司
items.example: The operator stopped the line for a safety check.
items.exampleCN: 操作员为安全检查停下了生产线。

items.meaning: to work together toward a shared aim
items.meaningCN: 为共同目标一起工作；合作
items.example: The two labs cooperated on the trial.
items.exampleCN: 两个实验室在该试验上合作。

items.meaning: in effect or ready to act; also a surgical adjective
items.meaningCN: 生效的、可行动的；也用于外科语境
items.example: The new rule is operative from January.

items.meaning: a work, especially a large artistic or musical work
items.meaningCN: 作品，尤指大型艺术或音乐作品
items.example: The symphony became his best-known opus.
items.exampleCN: 这部交响曲成了他最著名的作品。

items.meaning: able to be operated or used
items.example: The hatch is operable from inside.
items.exampleCN: 这个舱门可从内部操作。

definition_zh: 操作员；接线员；运算符；经营者
definition_en: a person who works a machine, a telephone switchboard or a service, or a symbol that stands for an operation in mathematics and computing
core_image: 控制台前一个人戴着耳机，把一排闪烁的推子逐个扶正
scene: 演播室外的控制台上，一个戴耳机的年轻人盯着指示灯，把每一路声音逐一推稳。The operator kept every channel balanced during the live broadcast.
sceneCN: 这里是「操作员」（第 1 个义项：负责操纵设备的人）；句意为直播时那位操作员让每个声道都保持平衡。图中可辨识物件：调音台推子、指示灯、耳机。

pos.zh: 操作员；接线员；运算符；经营者

derivatives.zh: 由拉丁语过去分词词干加 -tion 构成，义为「操作；手术；运算」
由拉丁语 operatus 进入英语，义为「运转；操作；经营」
由 operation 加 -al 构成，义为「运作上的；可使用的」

senses.title: A person who works equipment
senses.definition: someone who controls a machine, a vehicle or a piece of equipment as their job
senses.definitionCN: 以操纵机器、车辆或设备为职业的人
senses.example: The crane operator stopped the load when the wind rose.
senses.exampleCN: 风变大时，起重机操作员停下了吊运的货物。
senses.why: Latin operator means one who works, and English narrowed that to a person whose work is running a particular machine.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 operator 意为「干活的人」，英语把范围收窄成「专管某一台机器的人」。

senses.title: A person on a telephone switchboard
senses.definition: someone who connects telephone calls in an office, a hotel or an exchange
senses.definitionCN: 在办公室、旅馆或交换台为用户接通电话的人
senses.example: The operator put me through to the manager.
senses.exampleCN: 接线员帮我把电话接到了经理那里。
senses.why: Early exchanges were manual, so connecting calls was real work done by hand, and the general word for a worker became the job title.
senses.whyCN: 早期电话交换全靠人工，接电话线是真用手做的活，于是「干活的人」这个泛称就成了岗位名称。

senses.title: A mathematical or logical symbol
senses.definition: a symbol that stands for an operation, such as plus, minus or AND in a program
senses.definitionCN: 表示一种运算的符号，如加号、减号，或程序中的逻辑与
senses.example: In this expression, the plus sign is an operator.
senses.exampleCN: 在这个表达式里，加号就是一个运算符。
senses.why: In mathematics and computing an operation is a defined action on values, and the mark that triggers it takes the name of the one who performs work.
senses.whyCN: 在数学与计算里，运算是对数值执行一种规定的动作，而触发这个动作的记号，就借用了「干活者」的名字。

senses.title: A company that runs a service
senses.definition: a business that runs a service such as transport, tours or a network
senses.definitionCN: 经营运输、旅游或网络等服务的公司
senses.example: The bus operator added two night routes this year.
senses.exampleCN: 这家公交运营公司今年新增了两条夜班线路。
senses.why: A company that keeps a service running is, in the word's older sense, the one doing the work, so it too is called an operator.
senses.whyCN: 让一项服务持续运转的公司，按这个词的本义就是「干活的那一方」，所以它也被称作 operator。

intro.en: Operator is the Latin agent noun for a worker, taken into English with its meaning almost unchanged and then narrowed to particular jobs.
intro.cn: operator 是拉丁语里表示「干活者」的施事名词，进入英语时意思几乎没变，后来才收窄到各个具体岗位。

items.en: Operari meant to work or to have an effect, and it supplied the verb at the centre of this family.
items.cn: operari 意为干活或起作用，是这个词族的核心动词。

items.en: Operator was the agent noun: the one who works, a maker or a doer.
items.cn: operator 是施事名词：干活的人、制作者、行动者。

items.en: English adopted operator for a person who performs work, especially skilled or technical work.
items.cn: 英语借入 operator，指从事工作的人，尤指有技术含量的工作。

items.en: With the telegraph and the telephone, operator became the title of the person who connected lines by hand.
items.cn: 随着电报与电话出现，operator 成了手工接线者的岗位名称。

items.en: Modern English extends it to machine drivers, service companies and the symbols that trigger operations in mathematics.
items.cn: 现代英语把它扩展到机器操作者、服务公司，以及数学中触发运算的符号。

note.en: The look-alike group is the Latin work family that operator belongs to; the near-meaning group is other words for people who run or tend equipment.
note.cn: 形近组是 operator 所属、由拉丁语「干活」长出的词族；近义组是其他表示看管或摆弄设备的人的词。

entries.definition: To work, to control a machine or to perform surgery.
entries.definitionCN: 运转；操作机器；动手术。

entries.definition: The act of working, or a medical procedure.
entries.definitionCN: 运作的行为，或医疗手术。

entries.definition: Relating to how something works in practice.
entries.definitionCN: 与实际运作有关的。

entries.definition: Working, in force, or a person doing secret work.
entries.definitionCN: 起作用的、实施中的，或从事秘密工作的人。

entries.definition: A person trained to look after technical equipment.
entries.definitionCN: 受过训练、负责技术设备的人。

entries.definition: A person who repairs and adjusts machines.
entries.definitionCN: 修理和调校机器的人。

entries.definition: A person or device that directs how something runs.
entries.definitionCN: 指挥某事物如何运转的人或装置。

normalIntro.en: Operator is the person-shaped member of the Latin work family, so the mnemonics follow -or, the suffix that turns work into a worker.
normalIntro.cn: operator 是拉丁语「干活」词族中「人」的那一格，联想就沿着 -or 走：这个后缀把「活」变成「干活的人」。

normal.en: Operator is operari plus -or, the doer of the work.
normal.cn: operator 是 operari 加 -or，就是「干活的那个人」。

normal.en: Operation is the work itself, so operator and operation are the doer and the deed.
normal.cn: operation 是「活」本身，operator 与 operation 正好是做事的人与所做的事。

normal.en: A telephone operator works the switchboard by hand, which is why the title survived the machines.
normal.cn: 电话接线员靠手在交换台上干活，所以这个称呼在机器时代还留了下来。

normal.en: In a program, the operator is the sign that performs the operation.
normal.cn: 在程序里，operator 就是执行那个运算的符号。

normal.en: A tour operator runs the trips, so a company, not only a person, can carry the name.
normal.cn: tour operator 负责组织行程，所以不只是人，公司也能叫这个名字。

abstract.en: One person at a console holding many channels steady: work made visible as a pair of hands.
abstract.cn: 一个人守在控制台，把许多声道扶稳：活就这样变成看得见的一双手。

abstract.en: The word for a doer quietly became a job title, then a symbol on a page.
abstract.cn: 「干活者」这个说法悄悄变成岗位名，又变成纸上的一个符号。

abstract.en: Every machine that runs well has someone, somewhere, who knows its sounds.
abstract.cn: 每台转得顺的机器背后，总有个在某个角落听懂它声音的人。

examples.en: The operator kept every channel balanced during the live broadcast.
examples.cn: 直播时那位操作员让每个声道都保持平衡。

examples.en: The operator put me through to the manager.
examples.cn: 接线员帮我把电话接到了经理那里。

examples.en: The bus operator added two night routes this year.

sensesIntro.en: The core is a person who works; the senses split into equipment, telephone lines, symbols in an expression, and companies that run a service.

core.cn: 核心意象：一个人戴着耳机守在控制台，把一排闪烁的推子逐个扶正。

branches.cn: 吊车司机盯着风里晃动的货物

branches.en: hands resting on a console during a quiet shift
branches.cn: 安静的班上，双手搭在控制台上

branches.cn: 一个报出哪条线来电的声音

branches.cn: 一个加号在两个数上干活

branches.cn: 经营公交的公司印出的时刻表

intro.cn: 这个词由拉丁语表示「干活」的动词加施事后缀 -or 构成；同一词干随后又给出行为、形容词和符号的说法。

latinIntro.en: The Latin source is the agent noun of the working verb, so the word has meant one who works from the start.
